synopsis: For the heavy off-road braking function, the booklet identifies ISO 19014—not ISO 26262—as the governing functional-safety framework; ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 are road-vehicle standards outside this program's scope [f162, f2355, f12065]. Nevertheless, it recommends borrowing ISO 21448 and ISO/PAS 8800 perception-assurance concepts, with a safety-case skeleton realistically achievable by mid-2027 for a team starting in October 2026 [f12018, f829]. ISO/PAS 8800:2024, published in December 2024, addresses AI safety for road vehicles only, while ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024, published in January 2024, provides guidance rather than testing requirements [f2730, f2731, f2726, f2727]. Experts disagree over whether to exclude machine learning from safety functions or accept it through ISO/PAS 8800-style assurance, and the booklet found neither off-road/mining standards with ML clauses nor a separate ISO 19014 acceptance process for ML perception [f1125, f15303, f15304]. ISO 26262-8 tool-confidence provisions offer a reference regime, but clause 11 was confirmed only through contents and secondary sources; proven-in-use concerns element reuse, not simulator validation [f9758, f7703, f7579]. Important verification gaps remain: ISO 21448 and several other standards were not verified, ISO/IEC 42001, 23894 and 24029 were not verified in the ML-rules review, and the corpus characterizes ML safety standards as mostly draft [f4336, f2392, f2099].
